Overview

Why this session

AI is already part of how we work. Understanding it makes us better at using it, and better at questioning it.

  • AI tools are already in your daily work, like Copilot and Claude
  • Agents are the next step, so it helps to know what they are and how they work
  • Knowing where AI goes wrong matters as much as knowing what it can do
Confidential and Proprietary2

What is agentic AI?

From ask to hand off

Same engine. The difference is what it's allowed to do.

Ask and answer

GenAI

Answers your question from what it already knows. You read the answer and decide what to do with it.

Analogy Like asking a smart colleague a question across the desk

Goal and result

Agentic AI

Takes a goal, plans the steps, and uses tools to get there. It hands back a result for a person to check.

Analogy Like handing a task to a colleague who does the legwork and returns a draft for you to review

What is agentic AI?

GenAI versus agentic AI

GenAI chat (claude.ai, Copilot)Agentic AI (Claude Code)
You provideA promptA goal
It producesOne answerA result after many steps
Who drives the stepsYou, prompt by promptThe agent, within limits set for it
Where mistakes show upIn the answer you readIn actions it took
Your roleAskUnderstand it and question it

What agents can do

CompareCross-check reports and flag mismatches
ResearchGather sources and summarize
DocumentDraft or update procedures and guidelines
Clean up dataFix messy spreadsheets and merge exports
ScheduleWeekly digests and scheduled reports
Connect to appsPull from GitHub, Microsoft 365, and Atlassian, etc.
BrowseOpen web pages, read them, and fill in forms

What is agentic AI?

How an agent works

1

Goal

You describe the outcome

2

Plan

It breaks the goal into steps

3

Act

It uses a tool, like reading a file or running a script

4

Observe

It checks what happened

5

Hand back

It stops and hands over the result

6

A person decides

Nothing goes live without a person's approval

Steps 2-4 repeat, adjusting and retrying, until the goal is met

The agent proposes. A person decides.

Git and GitHub

Git is the undo button, GitHub is the review desk

Agents change files. Someone has to see what changed and undo it if it's wrong.

Runs on your computer

Git

Saves every version of your files, so you can see what changed and go back

Like version history in Word or SharePoint

Lives online

GitHub

A website where teams store their Git projects and review changes together

Like a change request board

Similar tools

GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps do the same job as GitHub

Confidential and Proprietary6

Git and GitHub

Five terms to read a change

Learn these and you can follow any agent's work

Repository

The project folder with its full history

Branch

A parallel copy to work on safely

Commit

A saved snapshot with a short note

Pull request

A request to review changes before they join main

Merge

Approved changes join main, the trusted version

Repository
main Branch Commit Pull request Merge
Confidential and Proprietary7

Git and GitHub

Who does what

In a safe setup, the agent prepares and a person approves

Agent
  1. 1

    Creates a branch, a safe copy

  2. 2

    Makes the changes

  3. 3

    Commits, saving a snapshot with a note

  4. 4

    Uploads the changes and opens a pull request to ask for review

Person
  1. 5

    Reads the diff, the before and after of every changed line

  2. 6

    Approves or sends back

  3. 7

    Merges, so approved work joins main

Every change is traced, so it can be reverted.

Risks and guardrails

Risks and guardrails

More autonomy means more guardrails, not fewer

RiskLooks like for usGuardrail in our demo
Wrong action
A plan to delete a device for a user on leaveAgent writes a plan. A person acts
Confident errors
A plausible but invented fact in the planA second agent reviews it. A person checks sources
Prompt injection
Hidden text in a ticket or email steers the agentTicket text is treated as data, not instructions
Too much access, including sensitive data
It reaches systems, personal emails, or employee IDs it never neededRead-only reviewer. An automatic check fails any pull request that changes data/ or CLAUDE.md
No trail
Nobody knows what changed or whyBranch, commit, pull request. Direct pushes to main are blocked

We'll try a direct push to main live. Watch it get rejected

Confidential and Proprietary9

Risks and guardrails

Five questions to ask any AI output

AI sounds confident even when it's wrong. These questions work on any AI answer, not just agents.

#QuestionExample from our work
1What did it read?Did it open the ticket and the Intune record, or guess from the title?
2What did it assume?"Inactive" may mean on leave, with Extension Attribute 9 left empty
3What breaks if it's wrong?A deleted device record is quick to redo. A remote wipe isn't
4Who's affected?The user, the manager, HR, a legal hold, a CEO direct report
5How do I undo it?Offboarded accounts restore within 30 days. A wipe can't be restored

A critical thinking exercise, 90 seconds

  • Device LT-0421, last check-in 78 days ago
  • Extension Attribute 7: Active
  • Extension Attribute 9: empty
  • Agent proposal: delete the device from Intune
  • Agent reply to user: "Your device has been removed."

Prompt: What did the agent miss?

The user is on extended leave. Record it in Extension Attribute 9 so the device is skipped next cycle. Don't delete.

Would you still trust the proposal from the start?

If you can't answer one, don't trust the output yet.

Setting the stage

Mocked up device remediation scenario

Four data files

inactive_devices.csv asset_register.csv offboarding_log.csv leave_list.csv

Two agents

device-investigator

Sonnet

Does: Cross-checks the four files, applies the CLAUDE.md rules in order, and proposes one action per device in output/action_plan.md.

Limits: Writes that one file only. Cannot edit data/ or CLAUDE.md, run commands, commit or push. If no rule fits: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW, never a guess.

action-reviewer

Opus

Does: Re-derives each action from the source data without trusting the plan's reasoning. Verdict per device is AGREE, DISPUTE or ESCALATE.

Limits: Read-only (Read, Glob, Grep). Never executes or edits anything.
